mainTopic: Why does רב נחמן rule כל דאלים גבר (whoever is stronger wins) in a dispute with no proof, when other cases with no proof end in splitting or in the judges' discretion?
overview: Just before this amud, רב נחמן ruled that when two people fight over a field and neither has proof, the court steps back and says כל דאלים גבר: whoever gets hold of it keeps it. The גמרא first compares this to two documents written on the same day, where רב says to split and שמואל says שודא דדייני (the judges decide). It answers that in the documents case the truth can never come out, so the court must give a final ruling. In רב נחמן's case, the truth might still come out, for example if someone brings witnesses later. The גמרא then challenges that answer with a משנה about a cow or a maidservant who gave birth around the time of a sale. There too the truth could come out later, yet the ruling is to split. The גמרא begins its answer with הָתָם, לְהַאי ('there, for this one'), and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Comparing to the two-documents case: split or judges' discretion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its challenge. In the two-documents case, רב says to split and שמואל says the judges decide. So why does רב נחמן say whoever is stronger wins?
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like what רב said there: they split it. And שמואל said: it goes by the judges' discretion. So why should רב נחמן's case be any different?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge that began just before this section. In another case with no proof, the court either splits the property or lets the judges decide, so why does רב נחמן let the stronger person take it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier case is two documents that give the same property to two people on the same day, so neither one is earlier. Neither רב nor שמואל says 'whoever is stronger wins' there. That makes רב נחמן's ruling look out of line with how the court normally handles a tie.

keyTerms.meaning: They split it: each side gets half.
The judges' discretion: the judges decide who seems more deserving.
Whoever is stronger wins. This is רב נחמן's ruling that the court steps back.

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of a sentence. The question ('what is different from two documents dated the same day?') began just before this section. Here you only see the end of it, which tells you what רב and שמואל ruled there.

phrases.english: where Rav said: they should divide,
phrases.notes: This is about two documents giving the same property to two people on the same day.

phrases.english: and Shmuel said: it goes by the judges' discretion?

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַב אָמַר: יַחְלוֹקוּ, וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: שׁוּדָא דְּדַיָּינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends a challenge that began on the previous daf against רב נחמן's כל דאלים גבר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling of כל דאלים גבר when neither side has proof.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the two-documents case there is also no way to decide, yet the ruling is splitting or judges' discretion, not 'whoever is stronger wins'.

steps.title: There the truth can never come out; here it still might
steps.stepSummary: In the two-documents case, nothing will ever clear it up. In רב נחמן's case, new evidence could still show up.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, there is no way to ever find out the truth. Here, it is possible to find out the truth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The difference is whether the truth could still come out later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With two documents dated the same day, nothing more will ever be learned, so the court must make a final ruling now by splitting or using discretion. In רב נחמן's case, one side might later bring witnesses. So the court does not make a final ruling and lets whoever is stronger hold it for now.

keyTerms.meaning: There: the other case being compared.
Here: the case we are discussing.
To get to the bottom of the matter and find out the truth.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up an important rule: כל דאלים גבר fits cases where the truth might still come out later, while splitting or discretion fits cases where it never will.

phrases.english: There, it is not possible to get to the truth of the matter;
here, it is possible to get to the truth of the matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the two-documents case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases: can the truth be found later or not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every case with no proof should be handled the same way.
steps.terutzMaskana: When the truth will never come out, the court gives a final ruling (split or discretion). When it might come out, the court applies כל דאלים גבר.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה of the animal or maidservant who gave birth
steps.stepSummary: A משנה rules that the newborn is split when buyer and seller argue about when it was born. So why isn't רב נחמן's case split too?
steps.simpleTranslation: And how is this different from what we learned in a משנה? Someone traded a cow for a donkey, and the cow gave birth. Or someone sold his maidservant, and she gave birth. One says, 'She gave birth before I sold her.' The other says, 'She gave birth after I bought her.' The ruling is that they split it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new challenge from a משנה in בבא מציעא. There, nobody can prove when the baby was born, and the ruling is to split it, not 'whoever is stronger wins.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 said: when the truth might still come out, the court uses כל דאלים גבר, and it splits only when the truth can never come out. In this משנה, witnesses could still show up and say when the baby was born, so the truth might come out, just as in רב נחמן's case. Yet the משנה says to split, which seems to go against the step 2 answer.

keyTerms.meaning: And what is different? The גמרא is pointing out a case that seems the same.
That we learned in a משנה.
One who trades one item for another.

phrases.english: And what is different from that which we learned:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in בבא מציעא 100a.

phrases.english: one who trades a cow for a donkey, and it gave birth;
and similarly one who sells his maidservant, and she gave birth –
this one says: "She gave birth before I sold her,"
and that one says: "She gave birth after I bought her" –

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רב נחמן, using a משנה that rules to split.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's כל דאלים גבר, read together with the answer in step 2.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In this משנה neither side has proof, and the truth could still come out later (witnesses to when she gave birth). By step 2's rule that should mean כל דאלים גבר, yet the ruling is to split.

steps.title: The answer begins: there, for this one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to explain how the משנה's case is different, starting with one of the two sides.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting its answer to the challenge from the משנה. The sentence breaks off here, and the rest of the answer continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word להאי ('for this one') begins a description of the position of the sides in the משנה's case. The sentence breaks off here, so the actual difference is explained on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: For this one, meaning one of the two sides.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the challenge from the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (the answer continues past this section).
